Definition: properly, to be fat, i.e. (figuratively) silly
BiblicalUsage: Kacal means to be fat, and so to be dull or silly. Jeremiah's charge against the idols is blunt: those who teach vanities are altogether brutish and foolish, fattened on what cannot save.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe folly fattens quietly: feed on idols long enough and the heart grows dull, which is why I keep my appetite on the living God.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
